title: The capacity model no longer has availability exceptions, since per-date vacation and flex entries replaced them
It no longer has clock intervals, since a weekday is a minute count inside one local day
Removing a per-date entry is an explicit removal
A working day never crosses midnight
A task is cancelled and a project is archived; nothing is deleted on request
Configuration carries a purge age in days, off by default; when it is set, a record whose cancellation or archiving is older than that many days is permanently deleted
Nothing is ever deleted while the setting is off
The moment of cancellation or archiving is recorded as a timestamp on the record, because the age is measured from it, which adds a cancellation timestamp to a task and an archival timestamp...
Purging an archived project takes its tasks, notes, time entries, and dependencies with it, and the setting's own description says so
Every purge writes a log entry
A batch raises an ephemeral notice naming how many records went and how old they were
The purge is not an operation anyone can invoke directly; it is a scheduled consequence of the setting
Removal asks for confirmation when, and only when, it changes something already reported: a per-date entry on a past date, a closed time entry, or a note
Plan-only removals, a future date entry or a task with no history, happen at once
The operation log keeps the removed content in either case, so the confirmation is about intent rather than recoverability
The review compares each past day's target minutes with the presence recorded for it, both recomputed from current configuration at the moment it is shown
No past itinerary is stored and no past itinerary is reconstructed
The limitation is stated in the interface: the review answers how the days went against the hours you expect of yourself now, not against the hours you expected then
Changing a weekday's minutes today therefore changes last month's review, and changing it back changes it back
The archive holds one JSON document carrying a header, with the format version, the application version, and the export time, followed by the stored records
It carries the identifier values and the sequence state so the data can be read without the database
When attachments arrive, they are included as a directory inside the same archive, so the layout does not change shape later
The format is documented and engine-independent
A backup is the database file itself, taken with VACUUM INTO or by copying the data directory while no service owner runs, as the specification allows
The backup restores the application, the export survives the application
The operation log is not part of the export
v1 exports, and it restores by backup, not by import
A dismissed ephemeral notice is deleted immediately
A finished or expired pending operation is deleted immediately
The dismissal record of a persistent notice is dropped together with the condition that created it
The operation log is kept forever in v1
Each migration runs in one transaction together with its version and checksum row, so a failed migration leaves the previous schema
The application refuses to open a database whose schema version is newer than the version it knows, rather than guessing
Before migrations run, the store writes a copy of the database beside it and keeps the most recent one
Per user and visible, as the specification requires and in each platform's conventional location: $XDG_DATA_HOME/workthread, defaulting to ~/.local/share/workthread, on Linux;...
The database, the confirmation code file, the most recent pre-migration copy, and the export default destination all live there
The ownership lock stays in the runtime directory
The task record gains a cancellation timestamp and the project record an archival timestamp, both of which the purge age reads
Removing a past per-date entry asks for confirmation, and removing a future one does not
The purge is not an agent-callable operation, and the export is
The data directory and the pre-migration copy join the storage decisions; the confirmation code file lives there too
The child that owns export and backup owns the zip layout, the format version, and the documented schema; the scaffolding child owns the data directory and the migration guard

section: Notes > New work and remaining fog
title: One thing is deliberately left to a later version rather than fogged: an import that reads the documented export, which the specification excludes from v1 and which the format now makes possible
